(p-274) Sūrat al-Takwīr

Its purpose is a severe warning of the Day of Threat, which is the final destination of travelers, because it is the greatest station for the manifestation of majesty, to those who denied that this Qur'an is a reminder for whoever remembers it, [recorded] in honored, exalted, purified scrolls, in the hands of scribes. The evidence that it is so is that its bearer is trustworthy among the Exalted Assembly, of established standing there, and the one who conveys it to us afterward is free from accusation and clear of any deficiency, because of what they knew of his condition before prophethood and what they used to testify to concerning his affair. He did not come to them afterward except with what is an honor to him and a reminder of what is within their own souls, in the horizons, and among the signs. That is sufficient [for them -] in judging that it is truth, and in certain knowledge that it is real. Its name is al-Takwīr, and the most indicative of what is in it of that is by reflecting upon the adverbial clause (al-ẓarf) and its response (jawāb), and what is in it of wondrous speech and its correctness, and what results from it of the greatness of the matter of this Qur'an.

(In the name of Allah) the One, the Subduer (al-Wāḥid al-Qahhār), (the Most Gracious, al-Raḥmān), whose blessing of creating and explaining [this Qur'an] encompasses the righteous and the wicked, (the Most Merciful, al-Raḥīm), who specially favored the people of His love with what made them happy in (p-275) the abode of permanence.

* *

When Sūrat ʿAbasa was concluded with the warning to the disbelievers [and the wicked -] of the Day of the Deafening Blast, because of their denial of the reminder that this Qur'an contains, this sūrah begins by completing that. It depicts that Day with the awesome matters that will occur in it, from the world of dominion and the realm of the unseen, until it is as if it were seen with the eye, as Imam Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Ṭabarānī and others narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ), through trustworthy narrators, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to look at the Day of Resurrection as if seeing it with the eye, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾." He began with the world of dominion and witness, because it is closer to conception with what prevails upon a person of attachment to sensible things, informing that it will be ruined, to renounce everything that drags toward it and to urge indifference and distancing from clinging to any of its causes: ﴿When the sun﴾, i.e., which is the greatest of the apparent signs of the heaven and the clearest of them to the senses.

Since the awe-inspiring matter is the absolute wounding up of it, which indicates the greatness of the one who winds it up, He used the passive voice, in the manner of the speech of those capable: His saying ﴿wound up (kuwwirat)﴾, i.e., it was wrapped up with the easiest matter, without any hardship at all. So it was made to enter into the Throne, as Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, and thus its spreading light departed. From "kuwwirat al-ʿimāmah," when you wrap the turban, so that some of it lies upon other parts, and some of it is obscured by others; and from "al-thawb," when you gather the garment and lift it up. So takwīr is a metaphor for raising it or casting it into Hell as an increase in the torment of its people, especially its worshippers; or it was cast out of its orbit, from a thrust, so that "kawwarahu" means he threw it in a gathered heap. The root denotes rotation, gathering and raising; for the sun, the verb is what "kuwwirat" indicates, because "idhā" requires a verb due to the conditional meaning within it. And since the effect upon the greatest thing indicates the effect upon what is less than it by way of priority, he followed that with his saying, generalizing after particularizing:

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 2:**

﴿And when the stars fall, dispersing﴾: that is, all of them, the small and the large, ﴿fall﴾, meaning they are thrown down, tumble, drop and scatter, until that happens as though by their own selves, without the action of any agent, in the utmost haste. Or it means they grow dark, from "kaddartu al-ma'" (I made the water turbid), so that "infakara" (it became turbid).

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him both) said: Allah will roll up (yukawwiru) the sun, the moon and the stars [on the Day of Resurrection] in the sea, then He will send upon them a dabur wind (a west wind), which will set them ablaze, so they become fire. Al-Kalbi and 'Ata' said: On that day the sky will rain down stars; no star will remain without falling.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 3:

When he began with the signs of the sky, because they are more well-known and more widespread in instilling fear and dread, and he mentioned from them two [of them] that are the most well-known among them and the most widespread in benefit, he followed them with the signs of the earth, saying, repeating the adverbial phrase (lil-zarf) for greater attention to the awe-inspiring: ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, i.e., those which, in the lower world, are like the stars in the upper world, and which are the hardest of what is on the earth. (p-277) He indicated the greatness of power by the passive form, so he said: ﴿are set in motion﴾, i.e., their moving came about over the surface of the earth, so they became like clouds in their motion and like scattered dust in their dispersal, so that the earth may be leveled and become a smooth plain (qā'an ṣafṣafan) in which there is no crookedness (ʿiwaj), because on that day nothing accepts crookedness in any respect whatsoever.

When he mentioned the inanimate signs, he followed them with the signs of the beneficial animals, which are the most precious of the wealth of the Arabs and the most prized, in a manner that points to the greatness of the terror. So he said: ﴿And when the pregnant she-camels are neglected﴾. That is, the she-camels whose pregnancy has reached ten months. ʿIshār (عِشارٌ) is the plural of ʿusharāʾ (عُشَراءَ), like nufasāʾ (نُفَساءَ) is the plural of nafsāʾ. They are the most beloved of the wealth of the Arabs to them and the most valuable in their sight, because they combine meat, back (for riding and carrying), milk and wool.

It was narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by his companions with a herd of pregnant she-camels, and he turned away from them and lowered his gaze. He was told: "O Messenger of God! This is our most valuable property, so why do you not look at them?" He said: "God has forbidden me from that," and then he recited ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to of them﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131], the verse.

That remains its name until it gives birth at the completion of the year. ﴿ʿUttilat﴾ means it is left unattended, as if it had no owner, although it is their most valuable property. So when it reached that stage, they treated it well, honored it, and their attention to it greatly increased, and they said: "Its best has come, of offspring and milk." This is because, with everyone preoccupied with himself, the matter is more terrifying than that anyone should turn to anything, however precious it may be.

And when the wild beasts are gathered (﴿وإذا الوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾). That is, the beasts of the land which do not become familiar with anyone, which one thinks are of no account and deserve no attention; so consider what the case is with others. ﴿Were gathered﴾, that is, were raised up and brought together from every direction by compulsion, for the purpose of presenting them before the Supreme King and of judging between them in their own selves, until the hornless one takes retribution from the horned one, and between them and others as well, until the sparrow is asked by its killer: why did you kill it? Qatadah said: every creature will be gathered for retribution, even the fly. End of quotation. And the wild beasts will not be startled by people, nor people by the beasts, because of the severity of the terrors, and that is more dreadful, more frightening, more fearful and more horrifying. Al-Qushayri said: It is not far-fetched that this may be by bestowing benefits upon them, as a permissible matter rather than an obligatory one, as the people of innovation have said. End of quotation. Everything in this world will be present in that abode; then, when the judgment takes place, the wicked will be placed in Jahannam as an increase in the punishment of its people, and the good will be placed in Paradise as an increase in the bliss of its people.

When he had made clear this gathering, he mentioned what points to the hardships the people of the station will endure from the intense heat, saying: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, that is, despite their vastness, ﴿are made to boil over﴾, meaning some of them are burst open into others until they become one single sea, and they are filled until what is in them exceeds their own volume, and they are heated until they become like the oven (tannur), blazing and roaring. Thus they become a drink for the people of the Fire and a punishment upon them. This cannot occur without there having arisen (p-279) from the heat that which melts the livers.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 7:

When he (Allah) mentioned two of the heavenly signs from the world of dominion (al-mulk), and four of the earthly ones, thereby making all creation understand that the matter is of utmost gravity, so that souls longed to know what He would do, He said, mentioning what He intended from the unseen world and the malakut (the realm of the invisible sovereignty), which consists of six matters corresponding to the number of the signs already passed from the world of dominion and witnessing, encouraging righteous deeds and righteous companions, lest a person be joined with what would distress him. He began with what is suitable to the folding up of the sun: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾, meaning, from every soul among humankind and others, ﴿are paired﴾, meaning, are joined to their bodies, and the gathering of each kind of creature with what its soul was accustomed to and inclined toward, so they became categories, as the Most High said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their wives, and what they used to worship﴾ [al-Saffat: 22] ﴿besides Allah﴾ [al-Saffat: 23]. And the coupling of the spouses is like the coupling of the sun, until its light is extinguished.

When the command was made clear, and hearts became hotter than burning coals, he mentioned what is the greatest purpose, namely the questioning, in a manner that understands the generality, and said: ﴿And when the buried alive girl is asked﴾ — that is, the children who were buried alive after birth, or in whom a cause of killing before birth occurred by means of medicine or the like. She was called al-mawudah (the buried alive girl) because of the earth placed upon her (p-280) which weighs her down so that it kills her. Wa'd (burying alive) is the inverted form of "adha," when it weighs heavily. Casting her into the pit dug for her is close to the dimming and falling of the stars. Since this was the lightest of killings in their eyes, and they used to think it was something of no consequence, He made clear that it is of concern and that she must be resurrected and made into one who understands and answers, even though the breathing of the spirit into her would take only a short time. So He said: ﴿was asked﴾ — that is, the question about what it is fitting for her to be asked about took place.

Then it was said, by way of a fresh sentence (istinaf), as a warning to the parents: ﴿For what sin﴾ — i.e., on account of what sin, O ignorant ones — ﴿was she killed?﴾ — i.e., she deserved to be killed by it in your eyes, while she [had not] committed any evil, since she had not reached the age of obligation. So what do you think of one who is above her, and of one who is a perpetrator of crime? Her question is by way of rebuking her killer. The Arabs used to bury daughters alive, fearing poverty or the shame that would fall upon them because of them, and they would say: "We return her to God; He is more deserving of her." Thus they did not accept daughters for themselves, yet they accepted them for their Creator. Among them were some who were too noble for this, and some who would ransom the girls who were buried alive and raise them. There is no evidence in the verse either for or against the punishment of the children of unbelievers, for the unbeliever who deserves eternal abiding (khulud) may be one granted safe conduct (musta'min), so his killing is not permitted, and the children have not done anything that would make them deserve killing. From the question put to the buried girl is derived the prohibition of wronging anyone and of restraining one's hand and tongue from every human being.

Since this indicates the generality of the question, he mentioned what arises from it, which points to bliss or punishment, so he said: ﴿And when the pages are spread out﴾, i.e., the sheets in which the deeds of the servants were written, ﴿are spread out﴾, i.e., they are separated and opened wide, laid open before their owners with the utmost ease. So the one who is fortunate will come to receive his [page] in his right hand from the direction of his face, in a manner that is a good tiding for him, while the wretched one will be given his [page] from behind his back and into his left hand, after it had been folded up at his death. Its spreading out is like the moving and scattering of the mountains. Whoever believes that his record is fixed, whether it will destroy him or save him, will find in it nothing but good, whether of speech, deed, or belief.

When he had mentioned what is unfurled and spread out, he followed it with what is folded up and gathered, so that what lies above it of wonders might become manifest and be looked upon. He said: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾, that is, this whole kind (of thing); he made it singular because the power over some of it implies the power over the rest. ﴿Is stripped away﴾, that is, is pulled off with a great force and an increased swiftness, and removed from its place, which is what covers it and encompasses it; or (it is removed) from the air surrounding its surface, which is like the spirit to it, just as a hide is stripped off from what covers and encompasses it, together with the intensity of its adhesion [to it], because that is the day of uncovering and manifestation. ﴿So We have removed from you your covering﴾ [Qaf 50:22]. And its stripping away (p-282) is like the uncovering of people from the pregnant camels and their scattering away from them. Thus whoever believes in its removal turns away from tying his resolve to anything of it, and entrusts all his affairs to its Lord.

When the obstacles were removed, the wonders of the creation appeared, which are the ultimate aims of the seekers and the final ends of the desires and the dreads. So He said: ﴿And when Hell is kindled﴾, that is, the fire of intense blaze, some of which is upon others and great, in a deep abyss, ﴿is set ablaze﴾, that is, it is kindled with a vehement kindling by the easiest of matters, and it is brought near to the disbelievers with utmost speed, so the matter is at the extreme of difficulty. This is close to the outcome of what occurs of terror from the gathering of the wild beasts.

When he mentioned the abode of the distant enemies as a warning, he followed it with the abode of the near, fortunate ones as an encouragement. So he said: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾, i.e., the garden of thickly interlaced trees and delightful meadows ﴿is brought near﴾, i.e., drew close to the believers, and they enjoyed the coolness of life and the goodness of the dwelling. Its levels were arranged and made ready, its pools and cisterns were filled, its vessels were adorned, its ground was cleaned and purified of everything that disfigures, and its meadows were made beautiful with everything that embellishes. From the statements of the lexicographers: al-zalf (with the vowel-movement on the lam): a water-skin, a level, and filled pools; and al-zulfah [...]: a cistern that has been made and filled, a dish, and upturned land; and al-zilf (with a kasra): the meadow. The meaning of this is the opposite of the kindling of the seas (sajr al-bihar). Thus the verse is an instance of al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which each of two parallel elements is left implicit where the other is stated): mention of the kindling (al-taf'ir) first indicates its opposite in Paradise second, and mention of the bringing near second indicates its like first. (p-283)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 14:

Since these things, by their awfulness, necessitate the gathering of concern and the turning of thought away from whatever occupies a person of adornment, diversion, play, or heedlessness, they necessitate knowledge of what is hoped for as bliss or what leads to the blazing fire. This also necessitates the hearer's eager longing to know what will happen. Then God, the Exalted, said, revealing that blessing through the governing element in "idha" (when) and what is conjoined to it: ﴿A soul will know﴾, i.e., each one of the souls. The indefiniteness here is like that in "a fruit of goodness from a locust" (thamarat khayr min jaradah). The indication of this awe-inspiring context regarding that necessitates certainty about it. ﴿What﴾, i.e., every thing, ﴿it has brought forward﴾, i.e., it has done and brought into existence. So it was fit for being presented, and its deed became a cause for the Powerful to bring it forth for it on that Day, preserved, with not even an atom of its good or evil escaping Him. Therefore, every person has a matter that concerns him, for there must be in his deeds what does not please him and what he regards as small in the presence of the Exalted, the Great. Whoever believes this desires that only what gladdens him be brought forth, and fears that what distresses him and harms him be brought forth. All these twelve enumerated things mentioned within the scope of "idha" are in the Hereafter after the second blast, as previously established in al-Haqqah, according to the apparent meaning, and it is a report from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, because the awe after the Resurrection is more fitting, more conducive to wisdom, and more striking.

The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When He, glory be to Him, said ﴿So when the Deafening Blast comes﴾ [Abasa: 33] ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother﴾ [Abasa: 34], up to the end of the surah, it was a likely occasion for the questioner to ask when the occurrence would be? So God, the Exalted, said: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ [al-Takwir: 1]. The occurrence of the sun's folding, the stars' falling, the mountains' moving, and the she-camels being neglected, all of that precedes a man's fleeing from his brother, his mother, and his father, up to what was mentioned up to the end of the surah, because what was mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Takwir is connected to the establishment of the Hour. So it is correct that this should be a sign of the first and a marker of it. — End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 15:

Since the context is one of warning (tarhib), and since it is most fitting for the end of 'Abasa that it should concern the disbelievers, and since the greatest of what the disbelievers commit after associating partners with God and denying the truth is the denial of the Qur'an, and that denial is what gathers all disgrace for the one who denies it, in His words ﴿Woe to man! How disbelieving he is!﴾ [Abasa: 17], the whole context of which concerns him. The one who denies it deserves this only because denying it brings him into every distress, even though nothing is more evident than it as the word of God, on account of its splendor, its gathering of rulings, legal judgments and knowledge, which none can gather in that manner and arrange in that order except God. Beyond all of that, it is inimitable (mu'jiz). Having drawn consequence from this warning, He says, swearing by that which indicates the great rank of the one sworn about, by leaving off swearing by things that are, in their own exalted station, of the highest majesty and magnitude: ﴿So I swear﴾, that is, for the sake of the truth of the Qur'an, because the matter concerning it is independent of an oath due to the intensity of its manifestness and the spread of its light. For this reason He pointed to defects that attach to these things He mentioned, while the Qur'an is free of every trace of deficiency, because it is the speech of the Most High King. So He said: ﴿By the stars that recede﴾, that is, the planets whose rising is delayed relative to the rising of the sun, so that they set in the daytime due to the overpowering of the sun's light over them. They are the stars possessing "anwa'" (mansions/risings) which they used to glorify by attributing to them the rains and the mercy that God sends down. They said: they are the Moon, then Mercury, then Venus, then the Sun, then Mars, then Jupiter, then Saturn. One of them has arranged them in verse, saying:

Saturn bought his Mars from his Sun,
so the Moon's bright lights blossomed for Mercury.

Then He replaced the first with the greatest of them and said: ﴿By the stars that recede, that run and hide﴾, i.e., the wandering stars that conceal themselves and disappear by day beneath the light of the sun, from the kanas of the wild beast (kanas al-wahsh), when it enters its kannas, which is its dwelling made of tree branches. Al-Razi said: the upper ones among them hide themselves behind the lower ones at conjunctions, just as gazelles hide in the kannas. Qatadah said: they travel by night and withdraw by day, so they are concealed and not seen. This is also narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Baghawi said: the root of khunus is returning backward, and kunus is taking refuge in their hiding places. Al-Qushayri said: that refers to their setting. He negated swearing by them only because, although they are great in themselves by reason of the benefits Allah, glorified is He, has attached to them, and you exalt them and go to excess regarding them, they have defects: eclipse and the dazzling of light. The Qur'an, for which the oath is sworn, is free of that. Rather, it is dominant over all other speech with a dominance greater than the dominance of the sun's brightness over the light of the other stars. Therefore it is not fitting to swear by them for its sake.

When he mentioned their disappearance, which implied the time of it, namely the day, he mentioned the time of their appearance, which implied their appearing. So He said: ﴿And by the night﴾, that is, the one which is the time of the appearance of the stars, the removal of their hiding and the going of their concealment, ﴿when it draws near⁠﻿ (ʿasʿasa)⁠﻿﴾, that is, its darkness approaches and its blackness and gloom gather, so the stars appear like scattered flowers in the wilderness of those dark shadows. For in it there is a decrease through the darkness and other rulings. It was also said: its meaning is that it turned back (adbara), and it was said: it grew dark, and it was said: it reached its midpoint, and it was said: it ended. ʿAsʿasa has the same meaning, and it is what does not change by reversal. This verse is of ihtibak (the rhetorical device of mutual omission): mentioning the hiding and the concealment of the stars first implies their appearance second, and mentioning the night second implies the omission of the day first.

When it might occur to someone that the darkness diminishes the fitness of the oath, he says, negating this: ﴿By the dawn﴾, that is, the most balanced of the times of the day, ﴿when it breathes﴾, that is, when it shines, its spirit and its breeze come forward, its comfort and its bounty, its light spreads, and its darkness is dispelled from the night by it. This occurs after the night has come and gone. That is, I do not swear by it, because although it has light, bounty, joy, delight and happiness, all of that diminishes beside the light of the Qur'an and what it contains of blessing and good pleasure. "And where are the Pleiades from the hand of one who reaches for them?" Moreover, its breathing is with coolness and gentleness, and the sun abrogates it with heat and density, whereas the Qur'an's breathing, with the breaths of holiness, the blessing of admonitions and intimacy, is not abrogated by anything.

[p. 288] When he had explained that these things, without which they would not have a pleasant life or enjoy existence, and which are of such excellence that only their Creator knows it, are too small to be sworn by for any of the virtues of the Qur'an, because of its immense status, which expression cannot convey and which tongue falls short of describing, he responded to that, informing of what is established in itself, a matter greater in its certainty than the reality of these things sworn by, guiding to the welfare of both abodes more than they guide, clarifying for the two envoys, the angelic and the human, upon them be prayer, peace, greetings and honour, emphasizing what the context requires, as it requires along with their denial, as a warning about the weakness of their intellects (p-288) and the greatness of their foolishness, after he had sworn by three oaths. The negation of swearing by them, together with their deficiencies, is like swearing by them, while showing that the one sworn to is far greater than them by an incomparable degree. ﴿Indeed, it﴾, that is, this Reminder mentioned earlier in ʿAbasa, possesses some of the beautiful attributes and sublime qualities it deserves, ﴿is the word of a noble messenger﴾, and he is Jibril, upon him be prayer and peace, whom We sent with it to the best of creation whom We created, and We made him a courier between Us and him, as wisdom required that. That is, that the essence of creation should have two aspects: one angelic, by which he receives from the angels, upon them be peace, since other humans cannot bear that; and another human, by which he receives from those to whom he was sent. It is known that the messenger's only function is to convey what he was sent with, so he is a pure envoy. And what was revealed, although it is his speech in that he uttered it and conveyed it without the participation of any devil or other, is without doubt the speech of God, because it expresses the eternal, inner attribute (the eternal speech of the self). Had the messenger's speech been independent in it, there would have been no place for describing him with the title of messenger, and eloquence would not require mentioning him by that description.

When he clarified, through the description of messengership, that it is not his own speech except insofar as he is sent with it and conveys it, and that in reality it is the speech of the One who sent him, he described him with what the description implies of what necessitates its preservation without any alteration or change whatsoever in any way, (p-289) and that is by clarifying his station with God, his honour, the explanation of his rank and the effectiveness of his word. So he said: ﴿noble﴾, meaning that all aspects of blame are removed from him and all aspects of praise are established for him. He is generous, of noble soul, manifesting the lofty qualities of character, free from any blame touching his court. Therefore he pours forth good by the permission of his Lord upon whomever He commands, to the worlds. He conveys what he was sent with exactly as it is, by his upholding the message in the manner of the honourable, so he changed nothing in it at all nor neglected, such that another could distort or alter it. Generosity (karam) is the gathering of the perfections proper to a thing.

Since this (quality) required strength, he made it explicit for emphasis, saying: ﴿Possessed of power﴾, meaning: [able to preserve] what he was sent with by himself, and able to repel others from introducing into it anything of deficiency. He reinforced the strength with his saying: ﴿with the Lord of the Throne﴾, meaning: with the Supreme King whose Throne encompasses all created beings, the One for whom, in reality, there is no "nearness" except Him. ﴿Esteemed﴾, meaning: possessing the utmost standing with Him, of very great rank, eminent in it. Thus he is such that no negligence whatsoever can come from him in conveying anything of what he was sent with, for conditions do not alter him, and the conflict of desires does not affect him, since he has no desire except what his Sender, glorified and exalted is He, commands him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 21:

(p-290) Since one who is firmly established in himself may not have helpers, He said: ﴿Obeyed there (in the heavens)﴾, that is, in the exalted assembly (al-mala' al-a'la), for they, peace be upon them, are the most obedient of all things to him. Al-Hasan said: God made it obligatory upon the people of the heavens to obey Jibril, peace be upon him, just as He made it obligatory upon the people of the earth to obey Muhammad (ﷺ). Since that implies trustworthiness, he stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿Trustworthy﴾, that is, supremely trustworthy (baligh al-amanah). He is one whose word is true, whose command is accepted, and who is relied upon in the matter of the message and the outpouring of knowledge upon hearts. He is spiritual (ruhani), purified in substance, action, and state. Whoever possesses these great attributes is such that he does not come except in a matter of the utmost importance, for kings do not send their confidants except in such a matter. For this reason God the Exalted entrusted him with His message.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 22:

When the royal envoy, who is Jibril (peace be upon him), was described with these five attributes, which removed from the Qur'an every ambiguity, and his being described thus was only to establish the nobility of the human Messenger, who stands between the Truth and the general body of creation, namely the Prophet (ﷺ), by the fact that what he conveys is the word of Allah in truth, and they used to describe him with what is utterly far from him while they knew this, He refuted them, rebuking them for lying and reproaching them for dullness, by saying, adding to his nobility since he was the one defending him: ﴿And your companion﴾, meaning the one whose companionship with you has been long, while you know that he (p-291) is in the utmost perfection, to the extent that you have no description for him in your eyes except "the Trustworthy." He intensified the negation and said: ﴿is not a madman﴾, meaning, as you attribute to him without shame before the manifest lie, together with the evident contradiction, the act of the basest of the vile. Rather, he brought the truth and confirmed the Messengers. So the Qur'an which he recites to you is not the speech of a madman, nor [the speech of] one of middling intellect, but the speech of the most intelligent of the intelligent and the most perfect of the perfect. This emphatic negation is established for him always, in an all-encompassing manner for every time. This is what the words indicate, not what al-Zamakhshari said, that it indicates the superiority of Jibril (peace be upon him) over the Prophet (ﷺ) and over the rest of the angels. For it was not intended for that, nor is it, by Allah, something that would please Jibril (peace be upon him). Al-Isfahani said here: "This indicates his virtue. As for it indicating that he is more excellent than all the angels and than Muhammad (ﷺ), that is not possible." And he said regarding the words of the Exalted in Al-Baqarah: ﴿and His angels and His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 98], that the mention of the angels first does not necessarily imply their preference over the messengers. As for the mention of Jibril before Mika'il, it is not far-fetched that it is for nobility, just as singling them both out for mention is for their virtue. And he said regarding An-Naba': ﴿Then he drew near to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic﴾, and this is the saying of Mujahid, which is supported by what is narrated in the hadith: "Indeed, the angel nearest to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Jibril (peace be upon him)." End of quotation. Had this hadith been sound (p-292), it would have been sufficient, but I have not found it at all. Al-Isfahani also said regarding ʿAmma, concerning the words ﴿the day the Spirit stands﴾ [al-Naba': 38], from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "It is the greatest of the angels in creation and the noblest of them, and the nearest to the Lord of the worlds." End of quotation. This, as you see, is explicit in preferring the Spirit. And al-Suhayli said, in his book Al-Rawd, concerning the Battle of Badr: "Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with a thousand angels; five hundred were on the right wing, and Mika'il (peace be upon him) was with five hundred on the left wing, and behind them was a reinforcement of angels who did not fight, and they are the thousands mentioned in Surat Al ʿImran. Israfil (peace be upon him) was in the middle of the line, not fighting as the other angels fought, (peace and blessings be upon them all)." End of quotation. This indicates the nobility of Israfil (peace be upon him), because his position is the position of the leader of the people, and his act is their act. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 23:

Since the madman does not truly establish what he hears or what he sees, the sense after this negation is: "Indeed he heard from Our Messenger to him what He sent him with, with true hearing, which was not confused for him, (in it) truth with falsehood." He then joined to it the report of his elevated status in seeing what no one else saw, and his trustworthiness, by His saying: ﴿And indeed he saw him﴾, that is, the one sent to him, who is Jibril, peace be upon him, in his true form on the night of the Mi'raj and at 'Arafat, combining the sense of hearing with the sense of sight ﴿at the clear horizon﴾, that is, the highest, which is near the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), where there is no confusion at all and no devil has any path to that place. So he knew him with true knowledge. And al-Baydawi said: "at the highest rising of the sun", meaning the place of the rising of lights, and "al-ufuq" (horizon) is the region that rises above and exceeds.

When the things that might be suspected—confusion in hearing and deviation of sight—have been ruled out, nothing remains except what concerns the conveying of the message, so He negates what might be imagined in that regard with His words: ﴿And﴾, that is, he did not hear it and see it while the matter is that he is not ﴿upon the unseen﴾, that is, the hidden matter, concealed from you, in transmitting it or in anything else, and this is a fortiori ﴿by a suspect﴾, that is, one accused—from ẓinnah (suspicion), which is accusation, as a soothsayer (kāhin) is accused because he errs in some of what he says. Thus he is worthy of being trusted in everything he says in all his circumstances. This is the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, al-Kisa'i and Ruways from Ya'qub with the letter ẓā' (ظ). But the meaning according to the reading of the rest [with the letter ḍād (ض)] is: not stingy, as a soothsayer is stingy out of desire for a reward (ḥulwān), but rather he is eager that each of his community should know everything that God Most High commanded him to convey.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 25:

When He had established for him (the Prophet) trustworthiness and generosity, after negating what they had slandered him with, and madness was more evident than the speech of a madman, because some madmen may at times speak coherent words (p-٢९٤) in [some - ] moments, so He negated that. And the speech of the soothsayer (kahin) was more evident than soothsaying (kahana), so He negated the speech, saying: ﴿And it is not﴾, that is, the Qur'an, which is among the totality of its miracles in reporting unseen matters, and He intensified the negation through emphasis with the particle bi, saying: ﴿the word of a devil﴾. Since the devil (shaytan) is never separated from being driven away, because his derivation is from shatana (to be remote) and shata (to burn), and that requires distance and burning, He described him by what is necessary for him, saying: ﴿accursed﴾, that is, stoned with curses and other meteors (shuhub) for the sake of eavesdropping (istiraq al-sam'), driven away from that, because the one who would speak to him is not a soothsayer, as you know. What remains of what they said is sorcery (sihr), and it does not need negating, because it is not speech; rather it is pure action, or speech accompanied by action. As for confused dreams (adghath al-ahlam), which are clearly defective (awar) for that reason, He did not repeat them. Whoever knows these attributes of the Qur'an and of the two messengers who bring it, the angelic and the human, loves it and loves them both, magnifies and venerates them greatly, devotes himself to its recitation at all times, and strives greatly in carrying out what it commands and fleeing from what it forbids, so that uprightness (istiqama) may be attained for him, out of desire for companionship with the one who brought it and for seeing the one who came from His presence.

When he left no way for anyone to cast doubt on him, through someone whose circumstances were unknown, ﷺ, he (God) made his words the consequence of that, rebuking and denouncing: ﴿Where then are you going?﴾ That is, with your hearts, away from (p-295) this clear truth, O people of Mecca, who claim the utmost acuteness, and you know this great preservation in the two messengers, the angelic and the human. So from where does what you claim of confusion in this great Book come, the Book which has shown its preservation by the proof of your inability to produce anything comparable to any part of it? This is a way of showing them to be misguided and foolish in the most eloquent manner regarding everything they used to attribute to it, such that their error became known with no ambiguity about it.

When the matter had become so clear that, if one alerts his companion with such a statement, the companion looks at it with the slightest glance, he said without pausing: "Where are you going?" He said: ﴿It is not﴾, i.e., what ﴿he﴾, i.e., the Qur'an which he has brought to you, ﴿is but a reminder to the worlds﴾, i.e., an honour to all creation, of jinn, humankind and angels, and a far-reaching, great admonition for them.

Since the whole of existence was honored by His manifesting Himself in it with a kind of honor, He released this expression. And since the one who is there is honored by the one who is guided, the admonition and the honor belong to him in reality. He said: ﴿For whoever among you wills﴾, that is, O you who are addressed, ﴿to go straight﴾, that is, to seek uprightness and bring it into being.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 81, verse 29:

When this was the case, the one who seeks to find fault (al-mutaʿannit) might rely upon it concerning the creation of actions (khalq al-afʿal). So He said, negating the independent ability of the creatures (li-istiqlalihim) and affirming acquisition (lil-kasb): ﴿And you will not will except that God wills﴾, i.e., O creatures, your willing is not independent, ﴿except that God wills﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, to whom no command belongs other than His own. If He does not will it, you are not able to will. So call upon Him, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, and He will will for you what pleases Him, so He grants you success in it. And on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, he said: The books which God sent down upon the prophets, peace be upon them, are ninety-some books. I read from them some eighty-some books, and I found in them: whoever attributes to himself any part of the will has disbelieved. End quote.

Whoever reflects upon this verse even briefly will know that the speech of the Muʿtazilah after it concerning destiny (al-qadar) is evidence that a person, when he has a desire (hawa) that nothing at all turns back, ﴿and whomever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾.

When He described Himself, glorified be He, as one from whose command nothing goes out, He followed that description with what is like the cause of it, so He said: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., the Originator of them, their Owner, the One who does good to them, the One who nurtures them, and He is more knowing of them than they are of themselves. Therefore they are not able except to what He has decreed for them, and it is obligatory upon each of them to obey Him and to turn wholly toward Him, glorified and exalted be He, and to thank Him, seeking an increase [of favor]. By this lordship His disposal of the sun and what follows it, of what was mentioned at the beginning of the surah, is valid, for the establishment of the Hour for the sake of the reckoning of creatures, and doing justice among them by severing all ties, as every lord does with whom he nurtures. How much more so with the Most Wise of judges and the Most Merciful of the merciful! Thus its two extremes meet in the most noble and most manifest manner, and the beginning of al-Infitar is arranged with its wondrous secrets. So al-Takwir is like al-Infitar and al-Tafṭir, and al-Inkidar is like al-Tasaqut and al-Intishar. And God, glorified be He, is most knowing of what is correct.
